# Area audit: using it

Step 2.106. Area 3 of [LEADS.md](../LEADS.md): "Each kind of person. They can do their whole job from start to finish on a phone without being told how: an admin sets up and runs a season, a scorekeeper finds and scores a game, a coach or captain sees their team, a visitor follows a team, a new person signs up and joins."

Written 2026-11-14 by the area lead for "using it", from the build branch at commit `c000569`. It changes no code and no plan.

## How this was done, and what was not checked

**How.** The web app was built once in the audit's own lane and run on its made-up stand-in (made-up leagues and people, no database, nothing leaving this computer). Five walkers on the strongest model each took one kind of person and drove a real browser (Edge, through the `playwright` package) from throwaway scripts, tapping what the screen offers and taking a picture and a text copy of every step. I walked the front door myself first, read all five sections, opened the pictures behind every High finding, checked each cause in the code, and judged the severities. Where a walker and I differed, the grade here is mine.

| Walk           | Who                                                                                                                                                             | Where                                                                                                    | Width                            | Pictured steps |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `lead`         | A visitor, the made-up member signing in, the owner                                                                                                             | `north-valley`                                                                                           | 390 × 844                        | 13             |
| `admin-setup`  | The owner setting up: finding the admin, every menu item, League settings, teams and rosters, the bin; once the admin of a draft league                         | `north-valley`, `harbor-city`, `quiet-pines` (draft), `old-meadow` (archived), `closed-gate` (suspended) | 390 × 844, then 1280 × 800       | 249            |
| `admin-season` | The owner running a season: the schedule grid, publishing, importing fixtures, game day in the games area                                                       | `north-valley`, `harbor-city`                                                                            | 390 × 844 (130), 1280 × 800 (21) | 151            |
| `staff-roles`  | A scheduler, a registrar, an editor, a club admin, a one-program scheduler, a scorekeeper on game night, a coach, a signed-in stranger                          | `north-valley`, `harbor-city`, `quiet-pines`                                                             | 390 × 844                        | 170            |

**Where the proof is.** Every picture, its text copy, each walker's own section and the scripts are in the lane folder `.local/lanes/2.106-using-it-audit/.local/audit-using-it/<walk>/`, which git ignores. Below, `admin-season/i05` means the picture in that walk's folder whose name starts with `i05` (a `.jpg`, often a `-top.jpg` showing only the first screenful, and a `.txt` with every word on the screen). Each folder's `walk.md` lists its steps in order and its `section.md` holds the full step-by-step table. **These files exist only in the lane folder: copy `.local/audit-using-it` to the main folder's `.local` before the lane folder is removed.**

**One thing was arranged so the new person's walk could go on.** On this computer nobody can read the 6-digit code the product "emails" (that page is step 2.96). A throwaway file loaded into the walker's own server (`known-code.mjs`, never part of the product) made every code 424242. Every screen, refusal and limit met was the product's own.

**What was not checked, so nobody assumes it.**

- **Whether what an admin does reaches the public pages.** On the stand-in the admin's teams, the public pages' teams, the games area's games, the schedule grid and the fixture import are separate made-up sets. A team added in the admin never appears on the site; a published schedule never changes the public schedule; a result never moves the standings. Only a game's own public page follows what is typed in the games area. This is the stand-in's limit, and it is itself finding M1.
- **Four of the six league settings.** "Start page for members", "who may score" and the two statistics settings save, and the stand-in's pages do not read them. A game "not theirs" under "only assigned scorekeepers" could not be met.
- **The live tracker.** In this lane `/{league}/score/{game}` is a placeholder. Lane 2.33 (its door) and steps 2.35 to 2.38 (its buttons) are not here.
- **Signing in through the form as staff.** The made-up owner, scheduler, scorekeeper and coach have no password; they were made "signed in" by their cookie and started from `/account`, where sign-in leaves everyone. Only the made-up member (who belongs to no league) used the form.
- **A game from before today, a corrected game shown publicly, a cancelled game on a public page, a tie, overtime, an archived league with games:** the made-up world has none. Finding H8 rests on the page's words and the code.
- **The emails themselves** (step 2.96), the invitation path (2.97), the real Google sign-in, the real sign-in service, the 15-minute lock running out.
- **Harbor-city's games area and import** (the stand-in has them in `north-valley` only), a league with several programs, a club's own teams.
- **Real phones.** Edge at phone size only: no iPhone, no Android, no Safari, no screen reader, no keyboard-only pass, no scripts-off pass. The laptop pass was made for the admin's jobs only, as the step says.
- **The look**, which is area 1's. A look fault is listed only where it stops or misleads someone.
- No unit test or gate was run; nothing in the product, the plans or the specification was changed.

## In short

| Job                            | How far a person gets today                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| An admin setting up a league   | **Stopped at the door, then at five more places.** No link leads to the admin: they must type its address. Inside, teams and rosters can be built on a phone. The league cannot be published, the season has no settings, people have no page, a wrong name cannot be corrected. |
| An admin running a season      | **The schedule: all the way. Game day: half way.** The schedule is built, changed, imported and published with a thumb. A final score, a forfeit and a box score work. A wrong score, a postponed game, a cancelled game and yesterday's game each end in a dead end.            |
| A scheduler                    | The whole job once inside, by a typed address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| A registrar, an editor         | None of the job: "Nothing here yet."                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| A scorekeeper on game night    | **Cannot find the game.** With the admin's address typed for them they can enter two numbers or a box score. "Open the tracker" is a blank page. They cannot undo their own mistake.                                                                                             |
| A coach or captain             | Nothing: no link to their team, no tools, and the admin refuses them.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| A visitor following a team     | **All the way, by tapping.** The live game page is the best thing in the product. They are misled by games whose time has passed, and left to guess what the short column names mean.                                                                                            |

Never asked their name.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

13 findings are High, 32 Medium and 12 Low. Section 6 asks the lead seven questions, proposes 30 steps, and proposes changes to 17 steps already planned and to the checks every page step carries.

The three things to act on first:

1. **The doors.** Nearly every screen that was built works when its address is typed, and almost none can be reached by a person. Sign-in leaves everyone on a page with no links (H1), a scorekeeper cannot find a game (H2), staff who are signed out are told they have no access (H3), and a wrong score can be corrected only by someone who knows the address (H5). The kept browser tests open each admin screen by its address with a sign-in cookie already in place (`tests/browser/schedule-grid-test.mjs`, `fixture-import-test.mjs`), so nothing has ever tested that a person can reach one.
2. **Game day is not safe from one wrong tap.** Two numbers typed in the wrong card end a game that is being scored live or is days away (H4); a refused save empties a whole box score sheet (H6); postponing and cancelling act at one touch and cannot be taken back (H9); the admin shows every game six hours from its real time (H7).
3. **An owner cannot take a league from nothing to a played season.** Publishing the league, the season's rules, divisions, rounds, people and inviting staff have no screen (H11), and nobody can watch any of it reach the public pages on this computer (M1).

## 1. What is finished

Each of these was used as its person would use it, on a phone, and does its job.

- **Looking needs no account.** Every public page of both leagues opens for a visitor. A parent gets from the home page to a team, its games, a box score and the statistics by tapping alone (`visitor/b01` to `b07`).
- **The live game page.** Score, clock, team fouls, the latest play and the players' lines changed by themselves within a second of each tap; "Show newer plays" works; the page turned to Final by itself; after a lost signal it caught up in about two seconds (`visitor/d03` to `d10`).
- **Every kind of game has a finished page:** postponed, forfeit, a score with no box score, no date (`visitor/e01` to `e06`).
- **Addresses can be shared and mistyped safely.** A team, a game and a filtered schedule open the same on a second phone; an old short name forwards and keeps the page; a wrong address inside a league ends on a finished page with "Back to the league home" (`visitor/i50` to `i52`, `j01` to `j14`).
- **The season picker** changes the page by itself and keeps the page and its other choices.
- **"My team" with no account** (U-5): one button, plain words, remembered by the phone, "League home" one tap away, undone with one button (`visitor/m11` to `m16`).
- **Children's names** in the youth league are first name and last initial everywhere, and "Names on public pages" there does exactly what it says, at once, and cannot be switched to full names by accident (`admin-setup/e09`, `ev01` to `ev08`).
- **Draft, binned and archived leagues** are shown or hidden as U-9 says.
- **The schedule can be built entirely with a thumb:** add, move, swap, remove, rename a round, change its date, choose a court. The draft is said plainly three times. Clashes are caught the moment they are made, in words that name the teams, the court, the day and the hour (`admin-season/c01` to `c16`).
- **The import's report** reads spreadsheet-style dates and names, and names every bad row with a reason a person can act on (`admin-season/f03`, `f08`).
- **A final score is two numbers and a tap; the box score** follows the season's statistics and warns while typing when the score and the players' points differ; **reopening with a reason** works. The game's public page follows at once.
- **Teams and rosters on a phone:** add a team with one field, add people with numbers and roles, change them, reorder, mark someone as left with a date (`admin-setup/f07`, `g06` to `g14`).
- **Two people saving the same thing** are handled as A-8 asks, in the schedule, a game and a setting.
- **Each role's menu is trimmed to what it may open**, and no menu offers an area that then refuses the person (checked for six roles). A league where a person holds nothing refuses every private address.
- **Making an account, signing in on a second device, staying signed in, a forgotten password, signing out and signing out everywhere all work.** A password change signed three other devices out at once. Coming back to a page after sign-in works when the address asks for it and cannot be used to send a person off the site (`new-person/b11` to `b21`, `m05` to `m11`).
- **Nothing was wider than the phone** on any page of any walk.

## 3. Findings

Severity as in LEADS.md. **High:** a person is stopped, misled or put at risk. **Medium:** must be fixed before real people use it. **Low:** tidying. "Step" names the planned step a finding belongs to, or says there is none.

### High

**H1. A signed-in person has nowhere to go.** (Finding H3 of the "nothing left out" audit, seen from the screen.)

- What the person meets: they tap "Sign in" in the league's phone menu and get a bare form with no league name and no way back. They sign in and land on "Your account": a device, "Sign out", "Sign out everywhere", and not one link. The front door says "Find your league, or start one. This page is not built yet." Back on the league, by typing its address again, the only sign of being signed in is that "Sign in" has left the menu. The owner must know and type `/north-valley/admin`. From the admin, "View the site" and the header's menu lead to public pages with no way back. Neither the admin nor the scoring page has a link to the account or to sign out: signing out on a shared gym tablet means typing `/account`.
- Proof: `lead/v04` to `v07`, `o01`; `new-person/m02`, `m03`, `b21`, `c08`, `c10`, `o09`, `k09`; `admin-setup/a01` to `a08`, `x03`, `x05`. Cause: the header's link carries no way back and draws nothing for a signed-in person (`apps/web/src/features/shell/site-header.tsx` lines 86 to 99); sign-in ends on the account page unless a page asked for the person back (`apps/web/src/server/sign-in/flows.ts` line 49); the account page has no links. The return itself works and is safe when the address carries it (`new-person/m05`, `q01`, `m06` to `m11`): only the links that should carry it do not.
- Should be: P2 lines 67, 71, 124 and 141. The Al-Hadi tracker does both today: its header shows a signed-in scorer "Sign out", and its "Scorer sign-in" link brings them back to the page they were on (`apps/live-stats/public/js/common.js` lines 159 to 171 and 247 to 250).
- Step: 2.127, not built. Section 6 lists what its line still leaves out.

**H2. A scorekeeper handed a phone cannot find the game, and the door to scoring is a blank page.**

- What the person meets: nothing on the account page, the league home, the menu, the public schedule or the game's own page leads to scoring. Told to type `/north-valley/admin`, they read "HOME. Nothing here yet." and must guess "Games". There, "Open the tracker" leads to "SCORE A GAME. This page is not built yet." with no game named and no way back; the same screen answers for a game that is final and for a game that does not exist.
- Proof: `staff-roles/ka01` to `ka10`, `kb01` to `kb04`, `kb21`; `new-person/k05`, `k06`, `k11`, `k12`.
- Should be: P4 line 65 ("A scorekeeper who opens the admin sees a list of their games and nothing else; games recorded live carry a 'Score this game' button"); P7 line 97. On the Al-Hadi tracker a signed-in scorer sees "Track live stats" or "Resume tracking" on every game of the public schedule (`apps/live-stats/public/js/schedule.js` lines 37 to 40).
- Step: 2.127 ("My games to score" in the account menu), 2.33 (the scorekeeper's list and the tracker's door, in a lane), 2.35 to 2.38 (the buttons). "Score this game" on the public schedule and on the game's page, where Al-Hadi's scorers find it today: **no step.**

**H3. Staff whose phone was signed out are told they have no access, and a signed-in person is told to sign in.**

- What the person meets: a scorekeeper or admin who opens their own page while signed out (a password change and "Sign out everywhere" both sign a phone out without a word) reads "You do not have access. This page is for the people who run this league. If you should have access, ask the league to invite you." At the gym they conclude the league took their access away. If they do tap its "Sign in" button they land on `/account`, not on the game. A person who is signed in and lacks the role (a scheduler at People, a coach at the admin) gets the same page, the same untrue words and the same "Sign in" button, which opens a sign-in form that does not say they are already signed in. The page never offers "Back to the league".
- Proof: `new-person/m12` to `m18`; `staff-roles/sa09`, `cax08`, `kb23`, `da02`, `da03`. Cause: one refusal page whose button is always a plain link to sign-in (`apps/web/src/app/forbidden.tsx` line 12); the gate already knows whether the person is signed in (`apps/web/src/server/league-gate.ts` lines 59 and 148) and nothing uses it.
- Should be: P2 line 106 (U-6); U-15 (decided for the founder in lane 2.33: a signed-out person is sent to sign in and brought back); DESIGN.md line 125 ("finished pages too … with one clear way on").
- Step: lane 2.33 for the signed-out half. The words and the way on for a signed-in person: **no step.**

**H4. One tap in Games makes any game final: one being scored live, one that is days away.**

- What the person meets: every game of the week, the LIVE one included, has the same two boxes and "Save final score" under it. Typing 40 and 38 under the live game and tapping once answers "The final score is saved."; its public page then says "No statistics were recorded for this game." A game two days ahead was made final the same way; its public page says "Played Tuesday, November 17", a day that has not come. Nothing asks "are you sure?". Two games at the same hour sit one above the other. A scorekeeper who does this cannot take it back (H5).
- Proof: `admin-season/g09`, `i05`, `iv02`; `staff-roles/ka10`, `kb13`, `kb15`, `kb17`, `kb18`. Cause: the list offers the boxes for any game that is scheduled or live (`apps/web/src/features/games-area/build-games-view.ts` lines 53 and 68); the command that records a final score never looks for plays (`packages/core/src/modules/games/commands/record-final-score.ts`), while the box score command does and refuses.
- Should be: P7 line 112 ("A game scored with the live tracker is refused here. It is corrected in the tracker, so its list of plays still explains its numbers"); P4 line 75 (A-5: "nothing important is lost by one wrong tap").
- Step: **no step.** Step 2.103 moves the button for looks only and says "What a screen does … stay the same". It needs an answer from the lead first (section 6, question 1), because tonight two numbers are the only way to record a live game.

**H5. A wrong result cannot be put right from any screen.**

- What the person meets: the owner saved 58 and it should be 59. The final game's card leads only to the public page, which has no pencil. The page that does the job exists, and "Reopen to correct" with a reason works there, but for a game recorded as a final score only, and for a forfeit, no link leads to it: the address must be typed. A scorekeeper who types it reads "This game is final. To correct it, reopen it with a reason; then fix the grid and save again." with no box and no button.
- Proof: `admin-season/h01` to `h08`, `h11`; `staff-roles/kb09`, `kb10`, `kb16`, `sc01` to `sc03`. Cause: the list links a final game to its page only when it was recorded as a box score (`build-games-view.ts` lines 69 to 72).
- Should be: P4 line 39 ("enter or correct a score") and line 14 ("a small pencil appears on things they are allowed to change (a score, …)"); P7 lines 158 and 159 (S-36: the scorekeeper may reopen within 30 minutes).
- Step: 2.56 (the corrections screen) and 2.120 (the scorekeeper's own reopen). Neither line says where the link is; the pencil on the public page has **no step.**

**H6. A refused save throws away what was typed.**

- What the person meets: twelve players' points and a score typed from a paper sheet, a tie by mistake, "This season does not allow ties. Enter a winner.", and the sheet is empty. The same on every admin form tried: the two score boxes, "Add game" (the form shuts and forgets the time and court), a round's name, a new team (name, short name, color and division all blank again, with "Something you entered is not valid" and no field named), a new person, a setting.
- Proof: `admin-season/k02`, `g03`, `b02`, `d04`; `staff-roles/kc02`, `kc03`, `kb05`; `admin-setup/f04`, `f05`, `g09`, `d09`. Cause: each form answers a refusal by sending the browser back to the page with a notice in the address, and the page is drawn again from what is saved (`apps/web/src/features/games-area/actions.ts` lines 22 to 23 and 55 to 56; `apps/web/src/features/schedule-builder/perform-action.ts` line 36; the teams and settings screens do the same).
- Should be: P4 line 73 (A-4: "If a save fails, the screen says so and keeps what was typed"). The plan's own page-step checks say the same (`STAGE-2.md`, "Steps", since the 2.105 audit): the screens ticked before that check was added (2.48, 2.51, 2.52, 2.54, 2.55, 2.64) were never gone over.
- Step: **no step.**

**H7. The admin tells the time six hours wrong.**

- What the person meets: Games says "Sun, Nov 15, 6:00 PM" for a game whose public page says "Sunday, November 15 at 12:00 PM". For a league in the United States a 7:00 PM game is listed at 1:00 AM the next day. A scorekeeper looking for "tonight at 7" does not recognise it.
- Proof: `admin-season/g01` against `gv02`; `staff-roles/ka10` against `ka07`. Cause: the games list prints times in UTC (`apps/web/src/features/games-area/games-page.tsx` lines 44 to 54); the import page has the same line (`apps/web/src/features/fixture-import/import-page.tsx` line 30, read, not walked).
- Step: 2.89 names it, tied to the games area's move onto the database. The time needs none of that: take it out and do it now (section 6). Not checked: whether a time typed into the schedule grid is taken as the league's own.

**H8. Yesterday's game cannot be found.**

- What the person meets: Games says "The games of today and the week ahead." and lists nothing else. A league that plays on Sunday and enters scores on Monday has no screen that shows Sunday's games: no "earlier" link, no date, no search. The admin's home, which should say "games finished without a final score" (P4 line 22), says "Nothing here yet."
- Proof: `admin-season/a04`, `g01`, `j08` for the words; the list starts at the beginning of the league's today (`packages/database/src/queries/list-games-in-window.ts` lines 71 and 72). Not walked: the made-up world has no earlier game.
- Should be: P4 line 39 and line 22.
- Step: 2.129 plans a "To do" line for "games past their start with no result", each "a button to the task". The screen that button must land on has **no step.**

**H9. A postponed game is a dead end, a cancelled game cannot be put back, and each takes one touch.**

- What the person meets: "Forfeit, postpone or cancel" opens three buttons one under the other, and each acts the moment it is touched. "Postpone" asks for no date; afterwards the card says POSTPONED and offers nothing, there is no list of games to reschedule, and the schedule grid leaves such a game alone. "Cancel the game" likewise, and a cancelled game has no button at all. The forfeit comes with the home team already chosen as "Team that forfeits", so one tap records a forfeit by a team nobody chose.
- Proof: `admin-season/i03`, `g08`, `i04`, `m01`, `m02`, `g05`; `apps/web/src/features/schedule-builder/schedule-page.tsx` lines 462 to 467.
- Should be: P7 line 80 ("A postponed game sits in a 'to be rescheduled' list until given a new slot"); P4 line 75 (A-5).
- Step: 2.53 plans the list and no more. Asking first, giving the new date, putting a cancelled game back and choosing the forfeiting team on purpose: **no step.**

**H10. A game whose time has passed with no score still says "Upcoming" and "This game has not started yet."**

- What the person meets: at 8:45 PM the 8:00 PM game reads "Starts Saturday, November 14 at 8:00 PM" and "This game has not started yet."; nine hours after a 10:00 AM game, the same. On the home page it sits under "Upcoming games", below next week's game. A parent asks one thing on game night: what was the score. In every league that types scores in afterwards, and for the demo league's untracked games, this is what they will read.
- Proof: `visitor/e05`, `m10`, `m01`, `b04`. Cause: `apps/web/src/features/live-game/build-game.ts` lines 65 to 68 and 123; `apps/web/src/features/schedule-pages/build-schedule.ts` lines 276 to 306.
- Should be: P7 section 8 (lines 196 to 204) makes "final scores entered later" a normal league.
- Step: **no step.** `STATUS.md`'s log for step 2.85 says this was written into step 2.147; it is not in that step's line, and it is a matter of what the page says, not how it looks.

**H11. An owner cannot take a league from nothing to a season.**

- What the person meets, in the order they would need it:
  - **Publish the league.** In a draft league neither the owner nor an admin finds any control or any word about publishing; an archived league cannot be un-archived (`admin-setup/o01` to `o08`, `n01` to `n08`, `q02`). P2 lines 128 and 130. Step 2.125 part 2.
  - **Settle the season's rules.** "Season settings. Nothing here yet." No game format, no statistics kept, no ties rule, no switch for jersey numbers: two players and two captains were given the number 4 without a word (`admin-setup/b11`, `g08`, `j07`). P7 line 9 calls this "the first thing an organizer settles". Steps 2.47, 2.138.
  - **Make a division.** The team form offers "No division" only and nothing offers to add one (`admin-setup/i01`). Step 2.49.
  - **Make a round.** The grid can rename a round and change its date and cannot add or remove one; no command to make a round exists in the code (`packages/core/src/modules/scheduling/commands/`). A new season on a real database will say "This season has no rounds yet." Not walked: the made-up seasons come with rounds. **No step.**
  - **Add and correct people.** "People. Nothing here yet." A person can be made only at the foot of a team's page, which also puts them on that team; there is no field for an email. A name typed wrong ("Jon Smiht") can never be corrected: a roster line has number, role, leaving date and order (`admin-setup/b04`, `g07`, `g10`). On Al-Hadi's own team page staff retype a name in place (`apps/live-stats/public/team.html` lines 25 to 28). P4 line 36; P6 line 59. Step 2.50; a small step ahead of it is proposed.
  - **Invite the people who help.** No Admins page, no invitation. P4 line 67. Step 2.97.
  - **Start the next season.** Step 2.130.
- The first demo walks a commissioner through exactly this, as a checklist "Before the first tip-off" from "Set up league identity" to "Confirm dates & publish" (`examples/alhadi-school/src/views/commissioner.js` lines 214 to 220). The admin's home here says "Nothing here yet." (step 2.129 for the home; the first-setup checklist is P4 line 26, which the "nothing left out" audit found in stage 5 of the build order).
- Step: as named for each. Rounds have none.

**H12. "It can be brought back" is not true: there is no bin.**

- What the person meets: removing a team says "The team is moved to the bin. Its games and numbers are kept and it can be brought back.", then "The team was moved to the bin." No area and no likely address holds a bin; the team's own address is "Page not found". The same for a person ("The person was taken off the league list.") and for a published game. As far as the owner can tell, one wrong tap lost a team and its roster, and the screen said otherwise.
- Proof: `admin-setup/h04` to `h11`, `g18`, `k06` to `k09`; `admin-season/e05`. The commands to list and restore exist (`packages/core/src/modules/leagues/commands/list-bin.ts`, `restore-team.ts`, `restore-person.ts`); no screen calls them.
- Should be: P4 line 75 (A-5).
- Step: 2.77, not built. Until it lands the words should promise nothing the owner cannot find.

**H13. In an adult league "Names on public pages" changes nothing, and the screen says "saved".**

- What the person meets: the owner of `north-valley` picks "Hidden: no names", reads "The setting was saved.", and every player's name is still shown in full, for all three choices. The screen shows "First name and last initial … (the default)" as chosen while the site shows full names, and asks the owner of an adult league to confirm what "the parents or guardians of the children in this league" agreed. An owner who wants names hidden believes they are.
- Proof: `admin-setup/d11`, `dv03` to `dv08`. The rule is followed (P6 lines 117 and 121, R-15 and R-24: in an adult league the setting acts only on people recorded as children, and no screen records that); what is missing is one true sentence, or a choice that works.
- Step: **no step** (2.146 repairs other things on this screen). It also needs an answer from the lead (section 6, question 3): the founder's principle is that the league is its admin's to run, and showing less is never the risk.

### Medium

**M1. Nobody can walk a season from start to finish on this computer.** The made-up world is four separate sets: the admin's teams (Lions and Owls of "Winter 2026"), the public pages' five teams of "Fall 2026", the games area's four, and the import's. So no one, the founder included, can add a team and see it on the site, publish and see the public schedule change, or type a score and see the standings move. It also ignores settings the owner saves ("who may score", "start page for members", the statistics settings), which then look broken, and it disagrees with itself: a team's record says 5-1 beside three results, and the home page's live game has a score and no plays. Proof: `admin-setup/section.md` section 1; `admin-season/dv01`, `f05`; `staff-roles/od01`, `kd01`, `oe01`, `cb01`; `visitor/b04`, `c02`, `d02`. Step 2.53's own done test ("publishing a change and seeing it on the public schedule") cannot pass here. Steps 2.93 (moving pages onto the made-up database) and 2.89 answer it part by part; no step says "one made-up world a person can walk end to end". Proposed step 30.

**M2. After a save, "Saved" is off the screen and does not say what was saved.** On the phone the confirmation was out of sight after 5 of 11 saves in League settings, after every save but the first in the schedule, and on a team's page: the line is at the top and the thing changed may be 2,000 pixels below, so the screen looks as if nothing happened. The words are the same for everything ("The setting was saved.", "The final score is saved."). Proof: `admin-setup/d06` to `d13` (each `-top.jpg`), `g08`, `s12`; `admin-season/c05`. Spec: A-4. No step (2.103 keeps what screens do). Proposed step 5.

**M3. Publishing the schedule asks nothing and does not say which games change.** The summary is counts ("Publishing will add 0, move 1, remove 1, and change how 1 are recorded. It reaches 4 teams and 40 people."); nothing in the grid marks a changed game and a removed one is simply absent; one tap publishes, with a team booked twice ("1 clash is still in the schedule."); the button is three screens down a long page; a blocker does not name its game ("A new game in the draft has no time."). Proof: `admin-season/e02` to `e04`, `d08`, `d09`, `c16`; `staff-roles/sd02`, `sd03`. Spec: A-7; P7 line 75. Step 2.53, with additions.

**M4. Removing is one tap with no way back.** "Remove game" sits beside "Save game" and acts at once. A player marked "left the team" by mistake cannot be put back: adding them again leaves a false "left on" line for good; a leaving date in 2031 is accepted. ### Low

**L1. The schedule grid has no dragging,** on a phone or a laptop, though P7 line 71 and ticked step 2.52 say "drag". The forms do the whole job and suit a thumb, so the gap is against the words. "Round name" is also the only door to the round's date (`admin-season/L04`, `d01`).

**L2. The games list marks neither today's games nor the scorekeeper's own,** has no day headings and does not say which team is at home; the data for all of it is there (`staff-roles/ka10`; `packages/core/src/modules/games/commands/list-my-games.ts`). Steps 2.33 and 2.129.

**L3. Nothing on a league's home page says a team can be made the start page,** and with "my team" chosen the team is not marked on the home page or the Teams list (`staff-roles/vb01`; `visitor/m12` to `m16`).

**L4. A club admin's refusal is dressed as a passing fault:** "The roster or the league list could not be read just now. Reload the page to try again." Reloading never helps (`staff-roles/cd01`).

**L5. Looking at a past season,** the menu puts a visitor back in the current one without a word, the picker on a team's page lands on the Teams list, and a finished season says "There are no upcoming games scheduled." (`visitor/f02`, `f03`, `f07`, `f13`).

**L6. A suspended league looks exactly like a mistyped address** ("Page not found"). Decided on purpose in step 2.87; a parent with a saved link will think the link is broken (`visitor/j25`).

**L7. Small untrue things on game pages.** A forfeit says "Played Saturday, October 24 at 7:00 PM" and offers "Box scores"; a finished game says "Played" with its planned time ("Played Sunday, November 15", shown on Saturday the 14th); a player who did not play has an empty row where Al-Hadi's page writes "DNP"; no gym address (`visitor/e02`, `d10`, `n02`, `e06`).

**L8. Small things that make a visitor guess.** After the phone's Back button the schedule's Team list can say "Owls" while every team's games show (Edge only); the ">" at the corner of a wide table looks like a button; the open menu closes only with its own button; a round folds again after Back; `/North-Valley/Schedule` is "not found" though `/North-Valley` alone is put right; note marks are 24 by 24; dates never show a year (`visitor/n05`, `n01`, `h03`, `e03`, `j14`, `c02`, `f07`).

**L9. Choosing a password: no "show" and no "type it again"** (`new-person/b16`).

**L10. Edge traps around sign-in.** Back after making an account shows "Choose your password" again, and saving there says "That took too long."; `/signin` and `/signup` show their forms to a signed-in person; "Forgot your password?" drops the page to come back to and has no way back; `/account/confirm` and `/account/inbox` open for a signed-out person; an unreadable device list is an empty heading (`new-person/b22`, `c02`, `c06`, `q02`, `m19`, `m20`, `o01`).

**L11. Small things in Teams.** A taken name answers "Another team of this season already has that short name." to someone who typed only a name; saving a setting with nothing changed turns "Now: the default." into "Now: set for this league."; the whole league list, with a remove button for each person, sits at the bottom of every team's page above "Remove this team"; "Page not found" inside the admin offers only the public home (`admin-setup/f05`, `d02`, `g01`, `h11`). Steps 2.50 and 2.90 should take the list off the team page.

**L12. For other areas.** Minutes typed into a box score are not on the public game page (`admin-season/Lv03`; area 6). The site's icon answers "not found" on the first page of every visit (with M21).

## 6. Proposed steps

The lead numbers these and adds them, or writes in the log why not. They are in order of importance. Every screen step also carries the page-step checks. "Needs" names steps by their present numbers.

### Questions the lead must answer first (each a "Decided for you")

1. **May a final score be typed over a game that has live plays, and by whom?** Recommended: no, while the game has recorded plays: it is ended in the tracker, as P7 line 112 already says for the box score. A game marked live with no plays may be made final by whoever may correct results, after a question. Until the tracker's buttons land, a live-recorded game that never started is simply scored as today.
2. **What does the public see while a result is reopened for correction?** Recommended: the result as it stood, marked "Being corrected", never "This game has not started yet."
3. **In an adult league, may the admin choose initials or "hidden" for everyone?** Recommended: yes. Showing less is always the admin's to choose and never needs a confirmation; only showing more of children does. If the answer is no, the screen must say in one sentence that adults are shown by full name. For area 5's lead to confirm.
4. **Does a youth league's statistics page rank children by fouls and turnovers?** Recommended: leaders for points and the other "good" statistics; fouls and turnovers stay in the tables and off the leaders unless the admin turns them on.
5. **Postponing: is the new date asked at once?** Recommended: offered at once, with "decide later"; the game then sits in the reschedule list.
6. **Where does "Sign out" leave a person?** Recommended: on the league page they were on (or the front door) with "You are signed out."
7. **"Creating an account" with an address that already has one:** recommended that the password screen, after the code has proved the mailbox, says "You already have an account. This changes its password and signs out your other devices."

### New steps

**1. "Score this game" where a scorer looks for it.** _For:_ Al-Hadi's scorers, who find "Track live stats" on the schedule today. _They will see:_ signed in and allowed to score a game, a "Score this game" button on that game's card on the public schedule and on its page; in the admin, their games with today's first and theirs marked, under day headings. Until the tracker is in, the scoring page names the game and offers "Back to the games" and what works tonight. _Done test:_ at phone width a scorekeeper on the league home reaches tonight's game ready to score in two taps with no address typed; a visitor sees no such button. _Needs:_ 2.33, 2.127. _Folders:_ `apps/web/src/features/schedule-pages`, `apps/web/src/features/live-game`, `apps/web/src/features/games-area`, `apps/web/src/app/[league]/score`. (H2, L2)

**2. A refusal that knows who is looking.** _For:_ staff whose phone was signed out, staff outside their role, a coach, a signed-in stranger. _They will see:_ signed out: the sign-in form with "Sign in to continue", then the page they asked for. Signed in without the role: who they are signed in as, true words for their case, "Back to {league}", for staff "Back to the admin", and "Use another account"; never "Sign in". A league that may not be shown to them stays "Page not found". _Done test:_ signed out, open a scoring address, sign in as the scorekeeper, land on that game; a scheduler at `/admin/people` reads that their role does not include this page and is back in the admin in one tap. _Needs:_ 2.33 (U-15), 2.127. _Folders:_ `apps/web/src/app/forbidden.tsx`, `apps/web/src/features/shell`, `apps/web/src/server`, `packages/site/src/messages`. (H3)

**3. Finishing a game asks first, and a live game is not ended by typing.** _For:_ a scorekeeper or admin with five look-alike cards on a phone. _They will see:_ the two boxes open only after tapping "Enter the final score" on one game; saving asks "Tigers 47, Lions 51. Make this final?"; a game days ahead says so first; a game with recorded plays offers "Score this game" and no boxes, and a final score sent for it anyway is refused in words. _Done test:_ no game can be made final with fewer than two deliberate taps; on a game with plays the list shows no "Save final score", and the game stays live. _Needs:_ question 1. _Folders:_ `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `apps/web/src/features/games-area`, `packages/site/src/messages`. (H4)

**4. Correct a result from where you see it.** _For:_ whoever typed 58 for 59. _They will see:_ "Correct this result" on every final and forfeited game in Games, and a pencil on the public game page, for those who may reopen it; someone who may not reads who can ("Only a league admin can reopen this game", and once 2.120 lands the scorekeeper reopens their own inside the league's time). _Done test:_ from the Games list two taps reach the reopen form; from the public game page, one; no address typed. _Needs:_ nothing for the link; belongs with 2.56. _Folders:_ `apps/web/src/features/games-area`, `apps/web/src/features/live-game`, `packages/site/src/messages`. (H5)

**5. A refused save keeps what was typed, and "Saved" is said where you are looking.** _For:_ everyone who saves anything in the admin; first whoever types a box score. _They will see:_ after a refusal every field still holds what was typed, the wrong field is marked and the sentence names it and sits beside it; after a save the words are on the screen without scrolling, beside the thing saved, and name it ("Saved: Tigers 58, Lions 61 is final."); a reload does not repeat an old "saved". _Done test:_ at 390 wide, type twelve players' points and a tie, save: the refusal is beside the scores and all twelve numbers are still there; add a team with the short name "Gym Rats!": name, color and division are still filled in and the short name is marked with its rule; save the last league setting twice in a row and read "Saved" each time without scrolling; add a third game in round 4 and see it and "Saved" on the screen. _Needs:_ nothing. _Folders:_ `apps/web/src/features/games-area`, `apps/web/src/features/schedule-builder`, `apps/web/src/features/teams-area`, `apps/web/src/features/settings-area`, `packages/site/src/messages`. (H6, M2)

**6. The admin tells the time as the league does.** _For:_ every staff member finding a game. _They will see:_ the games list and the import page in the league's own day and hour, written as the public pages write them; the schedule grid's dates the same ("Sun, Nov 22, 6:00 PM", not "2026-11-22, 18:00"). _Done test:_ a game at 7:00 PM in a league set to Chicago time reads "7:00 PM" in the games list, in the grid and on its public page, under "Today" on that day. _Needs:_ nothing (taken out of 2.89). _Folders:_ `apps/web/src/features/games-area`, `apps/web/src/features/fixture-import`, `apps/web/src/features/schedule-builder`. (H7)

**7. Games that still need a result, however old.** _For:_ the owner the morning after. _They will see:_ at the top of Games, "Needs a result": every game past its start that is not final, postponed or cancelled; under it Today, then This week; and "Earlier games" by round. _Done test:_ with a game dated three days ago and no score, the owner opens Games on a phone, sees it first, types two numbers and it is final. _Needs:_ a new list query; 2.129's "To do" button lands here. _Folders:_ `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `packages/database/src/queries`, `apps/web/src/features/games-area`. (H8)

**8. Postponed and cancelled games have a way on, and ask first.** _For:_ the owner and the scheduler. _They will see:_ "Postpone" asks "Postpone Lions at Hawks?" and offers a new date at once or "decide later"; a "To be rescheduled" list in Schedule and Games, each game with "Give it a new date"; "Cancel the game" asks first, and a cancelled game has "Put this game back" with a reason; "Team that forfeits" starts empty. _Done test:_ postpone a game, find it in the list, give it a date, publish, see it scheduled again; cancel one and put it back; a forfeit cannot be recorded without choosing the team. _Needs:_ 2.53; a command to reschedule and one to put back; question 5. _Folders:_ `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `packages/core/src/modules/scheduling`, `apps/web/src/features/games-area`, `apps/web/src/features/schedule-builder`. (H9, M32)

**9. A game that is past and has no score says so.** _For:_ a parent in any league that types scores in afterwards. _They will see:_ on the card a pill "Awaiting score"; on the game's page "Was set for Saturday, November 14 at 10:00 AM" and "No score has been entered yet."; on the home page and a team's page these games in their own short list, apart from "Upcoming games". _Done test:_ at 390 wide, after a scheduled game's time has passed, the game is not under "Upcoming games", its card says "Awaiting score" and its page does not say "has not started yet". _Needs:_ nothing. _Folders:_ `apps/web/src/features/schedule-pages`, `apps/web/src/features/live-game`, `apps/web/src/features/team-pages`, `packages/ui`, `packages/site/src/messages`. (H10)

**10. A player can still ask you to show less." and offers the three-way choice only where it can change something. ## 7. For the founder, in ten plain lines

1. A parent can open a league on a phone and follow a team from the home page to a box score with no account. The live game page updates by itself and is the best thing in the product.
2. A new person can make an account in three short screens, sign in on a second phone, and get back in after forgetting a password.
3. After signing in, nobody has anywhere to go: there is no link to their league, their admin, their games or their team. Every staff screen has to be reached by typing its address.
4. An admin who is given the address can build teams and rosters, build a schedule by hand or from a spreadsheet, publish it, and enter a final score, a forfeit or a box score, all on a phone.
5. They cannot publish the league itself, set the season's rules, add a round or a division, correct a misspelt name, invite a helper, find yesterday's game, or bring back anything they removed.
6. A scorekeeper cannot find tonight's game, and live scoring is not built yet. A coach has nothing.
7. Five things would change this most. First: after signing in, everyone sees their league and their work (already planned; open it now).
8. Second and third: a "Score this game" button where your Al-Hadi scorers find it today; and game day made safe from one wrong tap (ending the wrong game, losing a typed sheet, a postponement that cannot be given a new date, a score that cannot be corrected).
9. Fourth and fifth: the setup screens an owner needs before a first game (publish, season rules, rounds, people); and one made-up league in which you can watch a team you add and a score you type appear on the public site, which nobody can do on this computer today.
10. Nothing here needs you today. Seven small product questions are answered for you in section 6, each marked so you can change it.
